title: Control the Options: Get Others to Play with the Cards You Deal
hook: Valerie changes the grant menu before the board realizes the vote is already framed.
counterintuition: Power often hides in the setup, not the speech. Here the better choice is to shape option control before the visible contest begins.
tryThisNow: Before the next relevant conversation, write the one pressure word in play: option control. Then choose the smallest visible action that changes it.
keyTakeaway: Design the available choices so the decision happens before the chooser notices the frame.

breakdown.fastRead:
Pavel packs the radio in the foundry desk. The control choice looks small, yet it can shift mercy.

Trap feels fast for Pavel. It also gives the room a clean target.

Keep options close and plain. One clear act should change what others can do next.

If the radio move feels false or cruel, narrow it. Power lasts when Pavel leaves fewer loose ends.
breakdown.deepRead: Vera faces the same pattern in parent choosing between two bedtime routines both leading to lights out. The useful distinction is option control, choice architecture, menu. Apply the move through the setup, not through a generic speech.
breakdown.fullRead: Vivian sees the limit clearly in sales team offering contract packages that all include the needed service. The move helps only when it stays narrower than removing all real freedom. If it becomes a pose, it loses the practical force that made it useful.

ifThenPlans.plan: If a work decision exposes option control, then change the first visible artifact or sequence before making the argument.

If the move could become removing all real freedom, then narrow it to one concrete action and one clear limit.
